analysis.title: Owens Corning (OC) 3Q26 Recap: Moderation in Housing and Lack of Storm Activity Reflected in 4Q Guide as Margins Try to Find a Bottom
key_insights: GS keeps a Neutral rating on OC and expects the stock to stay range bound. It cites loss of operating leverage and limited visibility into 2027.

Three headwinds are named: no carryover in roofing because of weak 2026 storm activity, price/cost pressure as inflation rises ahead of volumes, and doors initiatives more than offset by the decline in new home construction.
Inflation is expected at $100+mn across the business in 4Q. Market share moves and weak demand are limiting price realization in roofing and insulation.
GS sees a slower start to 2027, with upside from there driven by the macro and by weather for roofing.
GS's 2026 adj. EBITDA margin estimate is about 500bps above the 2015-19 average in insulation and about 700bps above it in roofing, largely from price since 2020 and company initiatives.
GS models $675mn FCF in 2026 and $440mn in 2027. The remaining ~$250mn of the $2bn shareholder return target is likely pushed to 2027, and GS models $450mn of buybacks in 2027.

Roofing: second half volumes are expected down mid-teens y/y. Management guided to a high-teens decline in 4Q industry shipments despite an easy comp (4Q25 off 28% y/y), and expects channel de-stock into 1Q.
Roofing 4Q model: segment sales -8.9% y/y, volumes -10.2%, price +0.3%, then +2.2% sales growth in 2027. Price/cost is expected to be negative again in 4Q.

Half of the 3Q roofing margin decline came from weather and the rest from weak demand and channel de-stock. 4Q roofing adj. EBITDA margin is guided down nearly 650bps y/y at the midpoint to 19%, largely in line with GS.

Insulation: 3Q growth was led by North American non-res (data centers, reindustrialization, Mexico) and Europe. GS models 4Q sales +5.1% (volumes +5.4%, price +0.8%) and a 4Q EBITDA margin of 18.4%, down ~190bps y/y, then 20.6% in 2027.

Doors: half of the sales decline came from the divestiture of the distribution business (1Q26) and an Oregon components facility (4Q25). Pricing is effective in January, and GS expects gradual, limited realization.
Doors 4Q model: revenue -5.7% y/y with a 1.5% EBITDA margin. For 2027, sales -0.5% and margin down 130bps to 5.1%. Management targets $75mn of cost takeouts.
GS cut 2026 adj. EPS to $7.70 from $9.80, 2027 to $7.75 from $10.70 and 2028 to $10.30 from $14.60.
The price target rises to $137 from $128, based on 8.2x (from 7.3x) Q5-Q8 EBITDA, because near-term forecasts remain below mid-cycle norms.
Scenario analysis: upside case $162 (17.7x 2027 EPS), downside case $100 (15.0x 2027 EPS). GS sees balanced risk/reward.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised to $137 from $128 on a higher 8.2x Q5-Q8 EBITDA multiple while 2026-2028 EPS estimates were cut. Rating stays Neutral with 16.3% upside to the $117.76 price.

sector_views.rationale: Moderating housing demand, weak storm activity and rising inflation limit near-term upside. Recovery depends on the housing cycle.

earnings_insights: OC 3Q26 recap (reported 4 Nov 2026 per GS note): GS cuts 2026E adj. EPS to $7.70 from $9.80, 2027E to $7.75 from $10.70, 2028E to $10.30 from $14.60 (GS estimates, adjusted).

GS 4Q26 guidance-based estimates: roofing sales -8.9% y/y, roofing adj. EBITDA margin 19% (guide midpoint, down nearly 650bps y/y), insulation sales +5.1% with 18.4% EBITDA margin, doors revenue -5.7% with 1.5% EBITDA margin (GS model estimates).
Management guided to a high-teens decline in 4Q industry roofing shipments, mid-single digit insulation sales growth, a low-single digit doors EBITDA margin, and a high-teens insulation margin.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Weak storm activity and channel de-stock hit roofing volumes despite an easy 4Q25 comp (down 28% y/y).
Expected to weigh on insulation residential demand in 4Q.

risk_factors: Upside: ability to realize price, faster or more effective company-specific initiatives, and effective capital allocation including shareholder returns.
Downside: consumer weakness in bigger ticket R&R spend, a rise in raw materials costs (notably energy-related inputs) that cannot be passed through, and increased competition if peers seek share.
Inflation above $100mn in 4Q and transportation and oil-based raw material cost increases.
Channel de-stock into 1Q limiting pricing realization and operating leverage.
